source.title: GaDei: On Scale-Up Training as a Service for Deep Learning
source.authors: Wei Zhang; Min-Wei Feng; Yun-Hui Zheng; Yufei Ren; Yandong Wang; Ji Liu; Peng Liu; Bing Xiang; Li Zhang; Bo-Wen Zhou; Fei Wang

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper.
record.tranche_reason: It varies mini-batch size and reports model accuracy after a fixed number of epochs on natural classification datasets, bearing on V5 with a different set of workloads and accuracy measure.
record.gate_note: Figure 3 reports accuracy for four NLC datasets as mini-batch size increases from 1 to 128, with 200 epochs fixed. The text says large batches cause unacceptable accuracy loss in three of four cases and Joule and Watt do not converge on large batches; per-batch values are figure-only. Table 1's communication-interval results and other system performance results do not measure V5's batch-size condition.
record.test_reason: The batch-size experiments concern CNN sentence classifiers, whereas V5 names image classifiers and language models. Natural-language classification is not language modeling. The image-classification experiments report system scaling, without a batch-size comparison of held-out performance. Thus the study's results fit none of the supplied versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' batch-size conclusion: conservative settings, including small batches, are needed to serve diverse NLC datasets. The paper's broader conclusion is that GaDei supports these communication-intensive settings while accelerating training and maintaining accuracy, with fault tolerance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses IBM Watson NLC workloads and accuracy after 200 fixed epochs to study batch size; the original version concerns image classifiers and language models and held-out performance under specified batch-size and recipe conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and mini-batch size; the authors report different outcomes across datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: With 200 epochs and batch sizes ranging from 1 to 128, the authors report unacceptable accuracy loss in three of four natural-language classification datasets. They specifically report large-batch nonconvergence for Joule and Watt. Individual numerical effects are unavailable in the supplied figure text, and the evaluation split is unspecified.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing mini-batch size under a fixed epoch budget can reduce accuracy in CNN sentence classifiers using a conservative training recipe.

record.problems: The batch-size accuracy values are figure-only in the supplied text, with no uncertainty reported. The text does not identify which three of four datasets have unacceptable accuracy loss; it specifically names Joule and Watt as failing to converge at large batch sizes.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 reports accuracy under communication intervals CI=1 and CI=8, but CI varies synchronization frequency rather than mini-batch size, so it does not measure V5. Other runtime and system comparisons do not measure the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance of image classifiers or language models at fixed epochs, and recipe changes that mitigate those effects.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps.
Accuracy effects of removing memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The corrected row states indicate inability to establish a supplied claim version; they do not negate the reported NLC accuracy losses. Communication-interval comparisons and GaDei system-performance comparisons do not establish V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
Language models; comparisons across batch sizes beyond the reported settings; whether longer training, learning-rate scaling, warmup, normalization, or regularization changes the penalty.
Dropout interventions and their effect on held-out error.
Sharpness or other trained-network properties measured against generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
